The Court made the following:
JUDGMENT:

-
Challenge in this MACMA is to the award, dated 10.12.2015 in M.V.O.P.No.66 of 2014, on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-IX Additional District Judge, West Godavari at Kovvur ("Tribunal" for short), whereunder the tribunal dealing with a claim for compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- made by the petitioners on account of death of Naga Mohini (hereinafter will be referred to as "deceased") in a motor vehicle accident, which was occurred on 13.01.2014, awarded a sum of Rs.3,55,000/-.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-IX Additional District Judge, West Godavari at Kovvur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2) The parties to this MACMA will hereinafter be referred to as described before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3) The case of the petitioners, in brief, according to the averments set out in the claim before the tribunal, is that the deceased is their mother.
During her lifetime, the deceased used to earn Rs.4,000/- per month by doing tailoring works.
On 13.01.2014 at 2-00 a.m., the deceased along with petitioners 2 and 3 was proceeding on a motorcycle as pillion rider.

On the way, when they reached near Anjaneyaswamy statue, on state highway, Kovvur, one APSRTC bus bearing No.A.P.28- Z-4516 (hereinafter will be referred to as "offending vehicle") driven by its driver, first respondent, came from the rare side of motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and hit the motorcycle and thereby the deceased fell on road and received severe injuries and died on the spot.
Due to untimely death of their mother, they lost the moral and financial support in life and therefore, they filed the present petition for compensation.
4) The first respondent remained exparte.
5) The second respondent got filed a counter putting burden on the petitioners to prove the manner of accident, income of the deceased and their entitlement.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle.
Therefore, rider of motorcycle and its insurer are necessary parties.
As they were not added as parties, the claim of petitioners is not maintainable.

The petitioners are not the dependents on deceased and therefore, they are not entitled for compensation and ultimately prayed to dismiss the petition.
6) On the basis of the above pleadings, the tribunal settled the following issues for trail:
(1) Whether the accident occurred was due to rash and negligent driving of bus bearing No.A.P.28-Z-4516 by the first respondent?

Apsrtc, Rep By Its Vc Md, Hyderabad vs Maddipati Durga Hemalatha, E.G.Dist 4 ... on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183088573/
2 (2) Whether the petitioners are dependants on the deceased and whether they are entitled for compensation?

entities.text: Apsrtc, Rep By Its Vc Md, Hyderabad vs Maddipati Durga Hemalatha, E.G.Dist 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If so, the quantum and payable by whom?
(3) To what relief?
7) During the course of enquiry, on behalf of the petitioners, the second petitioner was examined as P.W.1 and Ex.A.1 to Ex.A.6 were marked.
No evidence was adduced by the contesting second respondent.

8) The tribunal on hearing both sides and on considering the oral as well as documentary evidence answered the issues in favour of the petitioners and against the respondents and awarded a sum of Rs.3,55,000/- towards compensation.
9) Felt aggrieved of the aforesaid award, the unsuccessful second respondent filed the present MACMA.

10) Now, in deciding the present MACMA, the point for determination is whether the award, dated 10.12.2015 in M.V.O.P.No.66 of 2014, on the file of the Chairman,
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal- cum-IX Additional District Judge, West Godavari at Kovvur, is sustainable under law and facts and whether there are any grounds to enhance the compensation?
POINT:-
11) Sri Aravala Rama Rao, learned counsel for the appellant, would contend that it was a case of triple riding.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal- cum-IX Additional District Judge, West Godavari at Kovvur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The tribunal did not look into the aspect of triple riding, as such, responsibility can be fixed upon the appellant and in support of his contention,
he relied upon a decision in United India Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. K. Anjaiah and others 1.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. K. Anjaiah and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He would submit that there was contributory negligence, as such,
compensation need to be reduced properly.

12) Mr. Lalith Kumar, learned counsel for the respondent Nos.1 to 4, would canvass a contention that the tribunal rightly dealt with the allegation of triple riding and it was a hit of the deceased by the APSRTC bus behind her back.
It is not the case of the appellant that the deceased lost balance and contributed to the accident.
The tribunal rightly dealt with all issues and awarded appropriate compensation, as such, award of the tribunal needs no interference.
13) As seen from the evidence of P.W.1, who was the second petitioner, he deposed the facts in tune with the pleadings.
Through his examination Ex.A.1 to Ex.A.6 were marked.
The tribunal considered the evidence of P.W.1 who was a witness to the occurrence and who supported the case of the petitioners.
As seen from the evidence of 2004(4) ALD 444 P.W.1 nothing was elicited to disbelieve his testimony.

sentences.text: 3 According to P.W.1 accident was occurred when they were proceeding on the left side of the road and offending vehicle hit the motorcycle of him in a rash and negligent manner.
For obvious reasons, the driver of the offending vehicle i.e., first respondent remained exparte.
The second respondent did not take any steps to summon and examine the first respondent.
There was no rebuttal evidence.
The evidence of P.W.1 remained unshaken during cross examination.

Unless the second respondent was able to prove by reason of triple riding the second petitioner lost control over the motorcycle and caused the accident, contributory negligence against the second petitioner cannot be upheld.
14) Turning to K. Anjaiah's case (supra), it was a case where the evidence on record proves the fact that there was a contributory negligence.
In the aforesaid circumstances, the High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad upheld the theory of contributory negligence.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Here is a case that police concluded the investigation and filed charge sheet against the first respondent alleging rash and negligent act.
Cause of death is on account of multiple injuries as evident from Ex.A.3- postmortem report.
Hence, the tribunal rightly held that the accident occurred was due to rash and negligent act of the first respondent.
15) According to the petitioners, the deceased is their mother and she used to earn income of Rs.4,000/- by doing tailoring works.
The petitioners are no other than the legal heirs of the deceased.
The tribunal negatived the contention of the petitioners that the deceased was earning Rs.4,000/- per month and arrived at monthly income of the deceased as Rs.2,500/-.
The tribunal was not inclined to deduct any amount on the ground that the income was arrived at notionally.
It is very difficult to accept such a theory.
However, the fact remained is that the very consideration of notional income of Rs.2,500/- when the deceased was a tailor who died in the year 2014, is lesser on side.

If the monthly income of the deceased is considered ranging from Rs.3,000/- to Rs.3,500/- per month in the year 2014 which is reasonable, after deducting one-fourth of the amount towards the personal and living expenses, the net drawings would be at Rs.30,000/- per annum.
So, overall income of Rs.30,000/- per annum need not be disturbed.
The tribunal applied multiplier 11 considering the age of the deceased and arrived at the multiplicand as Rs.3,30,000/- and awarded Rs.25,000/- towards transport and funeral expenses.

It is to be noted that in view of the judgment in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others2, conventional heads of compensation towards funeral and loss of estate is Rs.15,000/- + Rs.15,000/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Here the tribunal awarded only Rs.25,000/-, as such, it need not be disturbed.
The overall compensation of Rs.3,55,000/- which was arrived at by the tribunal was on reasonable basis, as such, there are no merits in MACMA.
16) In the result, MACMA is dismissed, but under the circumstances without costs.
The appellant shall deposit the rest of the compensation, if any, within a period of one month from this day.
Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
__ JUSTICE A.V. RAVINDRA BABU Dt.08.05.2024
